description: Data minimisation at ingestion. Each parsed trade mark record's applicant is classified by legal form before anything is persisted or enriched; only applicants whose type is in keep_types are stored. Sole traders, ordinary partnerships and private individuals are treated as individuals under UK GDPR/PECR, so they are dropped and only an aggregate count is kept. Set enabled to false to restore the previous behaviour (every parsed record stored).
_drop_unknown_note: An applicant with no legal form and no non-corporate marker cannot be classified from its name alone. Companies House matching runs after ingestion, so it cannot rescue these. Keeping them would re-introduce personal data, so they are dropped and counted under reason 'unknown' in the dropped-count log. Set to false to keep them (they are then stored and processed as before).
_foreign_corporate_forms_note: Incorporated bodies from other jurisdictions are legal persons, not individuals, so they are classified as limited_company. Matched only as the final word(s) of the name, because several of these ('sa', 'ag') are also ordinary words or initials.
_limited_partnership_forms_note: Checked after llp_forms and before limited_company_forms, so 'Limited Partnership' is not mistaken for a limited company. An LP is a partnership, not a company.
_partnership_patterns_note: Regular expressions, case-insensitive, applied to the raw applicant name. Only consulted when no limited-company or LLP form is present, so 'Smith & Co Ltd' is still a limited company.
_business_words_note: A name containing any of these words, or any word in exclusions.json natural_person_applicant.corporate_suffixes, is not treated as a bare personal name. Such a name with no legal form is 'unknown' rather than 'individual'. This only changes the reason recorded in the dropped-count log unless drop_unknown is false.
